subject: Production: MedixHealth - Westus2 latency blitz and geo-failover review
messages:
From: Samantha Brooks <samantha.brooks@medixhealth.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 14 Sep 2028 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Production outage - WestUS2 spike (5xx + tail latency)

Soojin / Vanessa,

We just saw a major spike in 5xx errors and tail latency for our inference calls routed to us-west-2 starting ~08:50 PDT. Error rate peaked ~18% for our live traffic; throughput dropped ~40% because requests timed out and retried. Our side already toggled to your fallback region but that added ~120ms median latency and a lot of user-visible slowness.

We need:
- Immediate confirmation this is on Redwood's side or something on the cloud layer
- ETA for fix or a recommended manual remediation (we're willing to accept a region swap if you advise)
- An ask for temporary credits if SLA is impacted; we will log an official ticket but wanted to escalate.

I attached a small sample of our request/response traces and session digests. Please advise next steps — this is impacting our checkout flow.

Thanks,
Samantha Brooks
Senior Platform Engineer, MedixHealth
Samantha.Brooks@medixhealth.com

Subject: Re: Production outage - WestUS2 spike (5xx + tail latency)

Samantha — thank you for the quick heads up and for including sample traces. We are treating this as P0.

Immediate actions in progress (internal bridge up):
- Rishi and infra are triaging K/V cache saturation and runtime metric anomalies (assigned)
- We will collect host-level diagnostics and request assistance from cloud provider if we see an infra fault
- Short-term: we may route a subset of Medix traffic to us-east-1 to restore throughput; we will only do so with your sign-off due to geo latency impact

Can you confirm you are comfortable with a temporary cross-region failover (us-west-2 -> us-east-1) for up to 60 minutes while we stabilize? We will:
- Notify you before we switch and again after we cut back
- Share a timeline and a post-mortem within 24 hours

We opened HubSpot ticket HL-2719 and attached your logs (link below).

Sincerely,

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 14 Sep 2028 09:27:00 -0700
Subject: MedixHealth P0 — proposed immediate mitigation and owners

Team — brief summary of what we see and suggested immediate playbook.

Observed:
- Error rate spike to ~18% for Medix in us-west-2 starting 08:50 PDT.
- K/V cache miss amplification on a small subset of models causing runtime backpressure and retries.
- Autoscale has been triggered but not fast enough for the hot-shard pattern.

Proposed immediate mitigations (please ack):
1) Rishi: enable aggressive prefix/KV caching and temporarily disable cross-shard livesync for the affected model group (5–15m config window).
2) Hannah: warm an additional dedicated pool in us-west-2 and increase burst capacity while we triage (target +20% capacity).
3) Vanessa / Soojin: request Medix permission for a controlled route to us-east-1 for ~45 minutes if caching + scale don't bring error rate <3% within 20 minutes. Communicate user impact and credit options.
4) Marissa: prep exec brief and postmortem template; start a timeline (timeline doc link below).

Why not immediate full geo-swap? The model has large KV state and swapping all traffic risks cache cold start-throttling in us-east-1 that might worsen 5xx for some sessions. A controlled percentage-based reroute is safer.

Please reply with a short ACK and ETA on each line item.

— Soojin
[Attachment: bridge_notes_initial.txt]

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 14 Sep 2028 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MedixHealth P0 — proposed immediate mitigation and owners

ACK — quick ops notes:
- Root cause candidate: K/V cache saturation causing multiple model shards to block on KV fetch; this amplifies latency and retries. Not seeing host hardware failures yet.
- Action taken: toggled aggressive prefix caching and raised KV cache retention for Medix prefix set. Throttles down from 18% -> ~6% in the last 5m.
- Monitoring: error rate trending down but 95p latency still ~820ms on fallback requests.

I recommend we do a controlled 30–45 minute reroute of 30% of Medix traffic to us-east-1 (gradual ramp) while we continue to warm caches in west. Benefits: immediate throughput relief and we can measure impact on tail latency. Drawbacks: increased median latency for those sessions and potential cost delta.

I'm standing by to execute with a hold-short if Vanessa/Soojin get Medix sign-off.

— Rishi
Director, Production Infra
Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Samantha Brooks <samantha.brooks@medixhealth.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 14 Sep 2028 09:55:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production outage - WestUS2 spike (5xx + tail latency)

Samantha — we are aligned and authorize the controlled reroute Rishi proposed.

We will:
- Execute 30% ramp to us-east-1 immediately upon your GO; escalate to 50% if error rate does not drop to <3% in 15 minutes.
- Offer Medix a one-time credit window for the affected hour; my team will follow up with your procurement lead.
- Schedule an executive sync at 11:00 PDT to review impact and next steps (I will invite Ops and Product).

Samantha, please reply with a one-line GO and we will start the controlled reroute.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Brooks <samantha.brooks@medixhealth.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, support@medixhealth.com
Date: Fri, 14 Sep 2028 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production outage - WestUS2 spike (5xx + tail latency) — actioning and update

Samantha — thank you for the prompt reply (and for the GO). We have started the step-wise ramp to us-east-1: initial slice ~30% at 10:10 PDT. Early telemetry: error rate dropped to ~2.3% within 6 minutes and throughput returned to normal levels. 95p latency for the slice in us-east-1 is ~350–420ms which is better than the degraded west path.

Next steps:
- Ops will continue cache-warm and monitor for 30 minutes, then we will gradually re-home live traffic back to west in controlled increments.
- Executive sync scheduled 11:00 PDT — invite sent to your team (link).
- Postmortem: we will deliver a timeline, root cause analysis, and remediation plan within 24 hours.

Attachments: small extracts of the bridge timeline and the traces we pulled (for your reference).

We understand the impact on Medix's customers and will make good on service credits if our postmortem shows we missed SLA targets. I will personally coordinate the executive follow-up.

Sincerely,
Soojin Lee
Account Manager, Redwood Inference
